Method: I made bare mirror clones (refs include GitHub PR refs and tags) and ran:
- sweep.py, which runs gitleaks git+dir plus the guard and denylist rules. The 12 gh GETs stayed under budget; core remaining was about 4,900.
- critic credscan.py and binscan.py.

  - deepscan.py: nested zip/gzip/tar/bz2/xz, rules inside archives, text over 2 MB, strings from pyc/sqlite. A synthetic nested whl>tar.gz test confirmed it fires.
  - extrascan.py: JWT, JWK d, private-key/seed/mnemonic assignments, eth/solana keys, Cloudflare, AWS secret, Twilio, SendGrid, Google OAuth, Fly, Resend, bearer and env-style secrets.
  - idscan.py: commit, tag and trailer identities; home-path usernames, hashed.
  - hits.py / mcat.py / maskmod.py: masked context.
  - lifescan.py: a private-life keyword sweep.
  - assetscan.py: GitHub release assets, scanned in memory.

Outputs:
- /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-macair/dff54175-f190-4444-a992-3cfe8aaacfa0/scratchpad/oss-audit/sweep/<repo>.json
- /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-macair/dff54175-f190-4444-a992-3cfe8aaacfa0/scratchpad/public-exposure/sweeper-b2/{credscan,binscan,deepscan}/, plus idscan.json, extrascan.json and assets-*.json

Gaps I verified in the critic's credscan.py (and so possibly in the private audit):
- A synthetic self-test showed it misses a tar.gz nested inside a zip or wheel, any bz2 file, and .pyc string constants whose 1-byte length prefix is alphanumeric. That covers strings of 48–57, 65–90 or 97–122 characters, so for example a 107-character Stripe live key in a .pyc would be missed.
- deepscan.py catches all three.

artbitrage:
- Its 612 big JSON versions (7.4 GB) were rule- and credential-scanned once as the union of their distinct lines. A secret that spans lines inside those versions would only be seen by gitleaks' diff scan.

The bare mirrors were freshly cloned on 2026-10-19 under oss-audit/mirrors and include refs/pull. Tools used: sweep.py (gitleaks 8.30.1 history+HEAD, guard+denylist rules, census), the critic's binscan.py, and my own scripts in <scratchpad>/public-exposure/sweeper-4/tools/, where <scratchpad> is the session scratchpad path the task gave. My scripts are: deepscan.py (critic credscan patterns plus recursive zip/whl/jar, gz, tar, bz2, xz, PDF-flate, zlib, UTF-16 and commit/tag messages), extscan.py (JWT, sb_, re_, Fly, Tailscale, age, Twilio, SendGrid, Tendermint privkeys, hex keys and mnemonics near key words, unquoted KEY=, Bearer literals), emails.py, homes.py, netinfo.py and lifescan.py; all of them hash values and print none. Every 'live-looking' verdict is shape-based; nothing was tested against any service. Not covered: GitHub objects reachable from no ref (force-pushed or dangling commits GitHub still serves by SHA), Actions logs and artifacts, the deployed agenttool-motifs Pages output, issue and PR edit histories, gists. Issues, PRs, comments, review comments and releases were fetched with 48 GETs (rate limit 4995 before, 4944 after; all counts under 100, so no pagination) and scanned: no hits, and no release has uploaded assets. Wikis: 0 refs everywhere. 7z and rar are not decompressed; none are present. Two tool gaps, both shown with synthetic fakes. (1) The critic's credscan uses trailing negative lookaheads (aws-akid, npm, hf, shopify, at_, telegram, brave, hex32-dot). These miss a value that is immediately followed by an alphanumeric byte, which is normal in pyc (a marshal type byte such as 'N') and in sqlite (adjacent column text). deepscan.py adds a relaxed pass for binary blobs. My batch has no pyc or sqlite (binary kinds: 94 PNG, 1 jar, 1 otf), so my results are unaffected, but other batches with pyc or sqlite should be re-checked. (2) The relational denylist matches line by line, so a pet name wrapped across a line break does not fire (love-bomb.sh lines 10-11). My masking lib adds a collapsed-whitespace pass. Personal content was found with keywords, the denylist and masked manual review; I cannot judge semantics everywhere. limits: Read-only. The only network actions were git clone (the sweep.py mirrors plus one upstream bare clone) and about 35 gh GETs: sweep's repo and actions-secret names, plus releases for 11 repos. Core rate limit was still about 4740. Wikis were probed with git ls-remote and none exist. Coverage: every blob and commit/tag object in every ref, including refs/pull, using: sweep.py (gitleaks 8.30.1 history and HEAD, guard and denylist rules); critic credscan (raw, gunzip, unzip) and binscan; extscan (tar, zip nested twice, bz2, xz, PDF streams); gitleaks git with --max-archive-depth=5. No archives, pyc, whl, jar, sqlite or tfplan blobs exist in this batch; the binaries are images, fonts, one .ico and one upstream .cbor. Nothing was tested against any service: 'live-looking' is judged from shape only. Placeholder judgements rest on entropy and shape, and the 'password' DSN value was confirmed by hash. Which person owns each commit identity is inferred: the icloud address and the aa1c2115 gmail are unverified, and author-name classes are heuristics on hashed names. The denylist only knows its 21 listed terms. Masking over-masks common words when terms span lines. Personal-life detection beyond the denylist is a keyword and ID-shape census, so it is not exhaustive.
